faq: Should I build login myself or use a service?
Services such as Auth0, Clerk, Firebase or Supabase Auth save time and handle security updates. We help you choose, or build your own with trusted libraries if you prefer.
Next.js, React, Vue, Laravel, Django, Rails and plain Node.js are common for us. Tell us your stack and we match it, so your team can maintain the code.
Do you store my users' passwords?
Passwords are stored only as salted hashes, never as plain text, and are never visible to us. Everything runs in your own project and hosting account.
Can you add this to an app that already has users?
Yes. We plan how existing accounts continue to work, then add the new login without forcing anyone to start over. The plan is agreed in writing first.
desc:
Sign-up and login for web apps and SaaS is the front door of your product: a registration form, a login page and a secure session. Ecom Swift LLC builds it in your own app with email, password and social login, matched to your design.

## What is sign-up and login?

Sign-up and login is the system that lets a visitor create an account, prove who they are on return and stay signed in safely. It includes the forms, the storage of credentials, the session that remembers the user and the rule that keeps logged-in pages private.

Every product with user data needs it. The question is only whether you build it carefully or patch it together.

## Why the front door matters

Sign-up is the first real task a new user performs. A confusing form, a vague error or a slow redirect makes people leave before they see your product. A login that forgets users too often frustrates the people who return most.

The back end carries the real risk. Passwords stored in readable form, sessions that never end and pages that check nothing are the usual causes of serious incidents. Building this part yourself from scratch is a common place to make mistakes, because the details are many and invisible.

## How a good login flow affects growth

A short, clear sign-up lowers the effort to start, and each removed field or confusing message keeps more people moving. Offering Google or Apple sign-in removes the need to invent and remember another password, which many people prefer. Returning users who stay signed in on trusted devices come back more easily.

Good error messages work as quiet support. "That email is already registered, try logging in" solves a problem on the spot. Redirecting a person to the page they were trying to reach, after login, keeps their momentum. Together these small choices help more visitors become active users.

## What a great sign-up and login includes

- A sign-up form with only the fields you truly need.
- Passwords hashed with a modern, slow algorithm, never stored as text.
- Helpful messages for taken emails, weak passwords and wrong details.
- Secure session cookies with sensible lifetimes.
- Logged-in pages protected on the server.
- Log out and a remember-me option.
- Sign in with Google, and Apple or another provider where you choose.
- Safe linking when the same person uses both email and social login.
- Protection against repeated password guesses.
- Redirect back to the page the user wanted.

## What we do

We confirm your framework, your design and your login goals. Then we build the pages, the server handlers and the session layer, and connect them to your user table or create one. We follow the conventions of your stack rather than adding unusual tools.

For social login, we set up the provider connections in your accounts and test each path: new user, returning user, and a user who signs up by email and later uses Google. We also test failed attempts, expired sessions and logout on several devices.

The Basic package delivers email and password sign-up and login with protected pages. Standard adds Google login, safe account linking, friendlier errors, redirects and basic guess protection. Premium adds several providers, invitation sign-up, a welcome step and a login history, plus a handover call and a short guide for your team.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Ask for as little as you can at sign-up.
- Let people see their password while typing.
- Keep error messages specific but not revealing.
- Test login on a phone before launch.
- Keep session lifetimes reasonable.

**Avoid:**
- Writing your own password storage routines.
- Forcing strict composition rules that people work around.
- Sending users to the home page after login regardless of intent.
- Asking for a long profile before they have seen any value.
- Leaving test accounts with weak passwords on a live system.

## Who this is for

This suits a founder whose prototype has no real accounts yet. It also fits an app that has a rough login and now needs social sign-in, or a business turning a public tool into a members-only product. Teams moving from a shared password to individual accounts will also find it useful.

## What we need from you

Send a link to your app or design files, the framework and hosting you use, and the sign-in methods you want. Please invite us to the repository as a collaborator and point us to a test environment. We never ask for passwords. For social login, you create or share the provider app in your own account, and we guide you through each step.
